title: Stability Handoff and Runbook Ownership Playbook
author: Maya Patel
content:
Summary:
This playbook standardizes how services at Redwood transition runbook ownership, how on-call handoffs are performed, and how runbook entropy is reduced. It is intended for SRE operators, service owners, and incident responders. The goal is to keep runbooks reliable, short, and actionable so first responders can stabilize services fast and confidently.

Scope:
- Applies to any customer-facing inference service, ingestion pipelines, and the runtime control plane.
- Covers handoff protocol, ownership matrix, pruning cadence, game-day exercises, and communication templates.
- Does NOT replace service-specific runbooks; it defines the governance and checks those runbooks must meet.

Key principles:
- Single source of truth: each runbook has one primary owner and one backup.
- Small, testable steps: every runbook action should be executable in 3–7 steps.
- Evidence-first: runbooks must document what evidence to collect and where to attach it in a postmortem.
- Entropy budget: runbooks age and must be pruned—we allocate an entropy budget per service.

Ownership & Roster:
- Primary owner: team responsible for the service (e.g., serving-runtime/team-name).
- On-call steward: SRE who validates runbook changes during the rotation (weekly steward).
- Backup owner: adjacent team with operational overlap (e.g., infra or platform).
- Roster example:
  - primary_owner: serving-runtime-team@redwood.com
  - oncall_steward: eng-sre-rotation@redwood.com
  - backup_owner: eng-platform@redwood.com

Runbook Metadata Requirements (must appear in the runbook header):
| Field | Required? | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| title | yes | "kv-cache-eviction-runbook" |
| primary_owner | yes | "serving-runtime" |
| backup_owner | yes | "eng-platform" |
| last_reviewed | yes | "2027-09-28" |
| slo_impact | yes | "p99 latency; availability" |
| evidence_bucket | yes | "s3://incident-evidence/kv-cache/" |
| severity_triggers | yes | "error-rate > 0.5% or queue-depth > 500" |

Day-to-day Handoff Procedure (30 minute standard):
1. Prior to handoff (10 minutes): primary on-call exports active alerts, long-running escalations, and mitigation locks to the handoff doc. Attach links to traces and dashboards.
2. Live sync (10 minutes): incoming and outgoing responders join #ops-bridge and run through: active incidents, mitigations, tentative root-cause hypotheses, and scheduled maintenance windows.
3. Acceptance + commit (10 minutes): incoming on-call owner confirms ownership in the roster system and updates runbook header last_reviewed field if changes were applied. If unresolved incidents exist, mark them with an owner and an ETA.

Handoff checklist (copy into calendar invite):
- [ ] Incident count and severity summary
- [ ] Open mitigation PRs/rollbacks
- [ ] Any scheduled capacity changes or maintenance
- [ ] Customer impacting tickets referenced
- [ ] Runbook header updated and linked

Runbook Pruning & Entropy Reduction (quarterly):
- Goal: reduce actionable steps by 30% and remove deprecated commands.
- Pruning cadence: owner performs lightweight pruning every sprint; steward performs formal pruning quarterly.
- Automated checks (CI): runbook-linter must pass: YAML header present, evidence_bucket reachable, and example commands return non-error status in dry-run mode.
- Decommission flow: when removing steps that touch infra, create a ticket with rollback instructions and run a shadow exercise during the next game day.

Game day plan (90 minute template):
- Objective: validate runbook step correctness and ownership clarity for a tier-1 availability scenario (KV cache saturation).
- Pre-reqs: test cluster with recorded traces and synthetic load runner.
- Agenda:
  1) 00–10m: kickoff, objective and success criteria defined (SLO impact simulation: p95 latency spike + p99 tail increase > 2x).
  2) 10–40m: inject fault (eviction storm) and observe signals.
  3) 40–70m: runbook execution by first responder; steward observes for missing steps or unclear evidence collection.
  4) 70–90m: retro and action assignment.
- Success criteria: runbook executed without >2 clarifying questions and mitigated to within SLO thresholds within 25 minutes.

SLO Thresholds & Escalation Triggers (examples):
| Signal | Trigger | Tier |
| --- | --- | --- |
| error rate (5m) | >0.5% (relative) | P1 |
| p99 latency (5m) | > 2x baseline | P1 |
| queue depth (instance) | > 500 | P2 |
| token-generation-failures | > 100/min | P1 |

Escalation ladder (automated):
- Alerting rule fires -> page primary on-call (P1 rules).
- If no ack within 3 minutes -> page backup on-call.
- If no resolution within 30 minutes or SLO breach persists -> escalate to on-call steward and senior on-call (exec pager).

Incident Evidence & Postmortem Linkage:
- Evidence to collect during incident: representative logs (10–20MB), traces (link to trace IDs), kernel metrics snapshot, and runbook execution transcript.
- Evidence storage: upload to evidence_bucket and tag with incident-{id}. Attach link in the incident ticket and postmortem.
- Postmortem template fields: timeline, mitigations, RCA, impact quantification (tokens, requests, customers), action items, owner, due date.

Customer & Internal Status Templates (copyable snippets):
- Internal bridge update (10m cadence):
  "BRIDGE UPDATE - {time} UTC
  - Incident ID: {id}
  - Impact: {services, regions}
  - Current symptom: {short summary}
  - Mitigation in place: {action}
  - ETA for next update: +10m or when changed"

- Customer-facing brief (email / status page):
  "We are currently investigating a partial degradation impacting inference latency for customers in {region}. Our engineering teams have implemented mitigations and are monitoring. We will provide an update within 30 minutes. We apologize for the disruption and will share a full incident summary after we complete our investigation."

Automation & Operational Tooling:
- runbook-linter (CI job): checks header presence, step count, and validates dry-run of idempotent commands. Failing runs block merge to main.
- stewardship-bot (Slack): posts monthly ownership reminders and prompts primary owners to mark runbook reviewed or schedule steward review.
- handoff-form (internal app): short form filled at end of live sync that creates a snapshot in /handoffs/YYYY-MM-DD/{service}.json with fields: active_incidents, mitigations, expected_ETA.

Runbook Health Metrics (tracked weekly):
- runbook_coverage_ratio: percent of services with runbook metadata complete (target 100%).
- average_step_count: median number of actionable steps (target: 5 steps).
- stale_runbook_count: runbooks not reviewed in 90 days (target: 0).

Periodic Review Cadence:
- Weekly: on-call steward spot-checks two runbooks in rotation and reports findings to eng-sre-retro.
- Quarterly: owners must complete pruning ticket and confirm game-day participation.
- Post-incident: runbook updates required within 7 days of a P1 with annotated evidence.

Appendix A — Runbook Header Template (copy this into new runbooks):
---
title: <short-dash-name>
primary_owner: <team>
backup_owner: <team>
last_reviewed: YYYY-MM-DD
slo_impact: <short note>
evidence_bucket: s3://incident-evidence/<service>/
severity_triggers: <list>
---

Appendix B — Useful commands (examples):
- Check queue depth: kubectl -n serving-runtime exec -it pod/ingress-0 -- /bin/bash -c "redis-cli LLEN inference-queue"
- Trigger cache clear (dry-run flag supported): ./scripts/cache-clear --service kv-store --dry-run
- Collect kernel metrics snapshot: /usr/local/bin/collect-kernel-metrics --out /tmp/metrics-$(date +%s).json
